heading: Knight moves = shortest path problem
body:
Chess knight on infinite board → **graph search**. Each cell is a node, knight moves = edges.

**Why BFS?** Explores level-by-level. First time you hit the target = minimum moves guaranteed.

heading: Symmetry cuts 75% of work
body:
Knight moves are **symmetric** across all 4 quadrants.

Work with `abs(x)` and `abs(y)` → search only positive quadrant → ~75% fewer cells explored.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why is BFS the correct algorithm for this problem instead of DFS?
options: BFS uses less memory than DFS
BFS explores level-by-level, guaranteeing the first path found is the shortest
BFS is faster than DFS in all cases
explain: BFS explores level-by-level by distance. First time it hits the target = shortest path guaranteed.
